references.text: Moses exhorts the people to choose life by loving the Lord, walking in His ways, and keeping His commandments, which resonates with the question of doing good for eternal life.
The Preacher concludes that man's whole duty is to fear God and keep His commandments, reflecting the idea of doing good to attain eternal life.
Jesus speaks about the significance and fulfillment of the Law, which is relevant to the question of doing good.
The Golden Rule, which summarizes the Law and the Prophets, relates to the idea of doing good to others.
The parable of the Good Samaritan, which answers the question of who one's neighbor is and emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds.
A similar event where a rich young man asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life, directly mirroring the account in Matthew 19:16.
Paul's teaching that the entire Law is fulfilled in one word, namely to love your neighbor, which relates to the question of doing good.
